list.label: On start of scene
list.description: Runs once when the scene starts.

list.label: On loading complete
list.hint: On a loading screen: everything the game needs is loaded. Go to a scene here, or wait for a tap first

list.label: On end of scene
list.description: Runs once when the scene ends (changing or restarting scene).

list.label: Every tick
list.description: True every frame (about 60 times per second).

list.label: Every X seconds
list.description: True once every few seconds.

list.label: Compare variable
list.description: Compare a global or scene variable with a value.

list.label: Compare two values
list.description: Compare any two expressions, e.g. Player.x > 10.

list.label: Is true
list.description: True when the expression is true (or not 0).

list.label: Is between
list.description: True when a value is between min and max (inclusive).

list.label: Random chance
list.description: True randomly, e.g. 25 = one time in four.

list.label: Raycast
list.description: Shoots an invisible ray from a point in a direction and is true when it hits something solid. Afterwards, in the actions of the same event, use rayHitX / rayHitY / rayHitZ (where it hit), rayNormalX / rayNormalY / rayNormalZ (which way the surface faces; rayNormalY is 1 on flat ground), rayDistance (meters) and rayhitname() (the object's name). Must hit makes the condition true only when the ray hits that kind of object, and picks it for the actions. Only tag ignores everything without that tag. Ignore lets the ray pass through those objects. Triggers (coins, checkpoints) never block a ray.

list.label: Trigger once while true
list.description: Put last: the event runs only once each time the other conditions become true.

list.label: Group is active
list.description: True if the event group is active.

list.label: Repeat
list.description: Runs the actions and sub-events several times. Use loopIndex for the current number.

list.label: For
list.description: Repeats the rest of the event, counting from start to end (both included). Use loopindex("name") for the current number.

list.label: While
list.description: Repeats the rest of the event as long as the conditions after it are true (or until "Stop loop").

list.label: On timer finished
list.description: True at the moment a timer started with "Start timer" runs out.

list.label: Timer is running
list.description: True while a timer is counting down.

list.label: Compare scene time
list.description: Compare the seconds since the scene started.

list.label: Set variable
list.description: Change the value of a global or scene variable.

list.label: Add to variable
list.description: Increase a variable (text variables get the value appended).

list.label: Subtract from variable
list.description: Decrease a number variable.

list.label: Toggle variable
list.description: Flip a true/false variable.

list.label: Go to scene
list.description: Switch to another scene.

list.label: Restart scene
list.description: Start the current scene again from the beginning.

list.label: Wait
list.description: Pause the rest of this event (next actions and sub-events) for a while.

list.label: Wait for previous actions
list.display: Wait for previous actions to complete
list.description: Pause the rest of this event until what the actions above it started has finished: a Tween, a Move to position, a play-once animation. Then the next actions run, e.g. slide a panel in, wait, then show its text. Nothing to wait for means no pause. An object destroyed or a tween stopped meanwhile counts as finished.

list.label: Wait until
list.description: Pause the rest of this event (next actions and sub-events) until the expression is true, e.g. Score >= 10 or Door.y > 5. It is checked every tick. If it is already true the event goes on at once. Careful: in an event that runs every tick, a condition that never comes true keeps adding waits.

list.label: Show message
list.description: Show a short message on screen.

list.label: Log to console
list.description: Write a line to the debug console (🐞 button while playing) without showing it in the game. Great for checking that an event runs, e.g. "Clicked! score = " + Score.

list.label: Show alert
list.description: Pop up a message box and pause until it is closed. Use it for one-off checks, not every tick.

list.label: Call function
list.description: Run a function block (made with Add → Function) with values for its parameters.

list.label: Set return value
list.description: Inside a function: the value that Functions.Name(...) gives back.

list.label: Stop loop
list.description: End the loop this event is in (Repeat, For, For each, While) after the current repeat.

list.label: Set time scale
list.description: 1 = normal speed, 0.5 = slow motion, 2 = double speed.

list.label: Vibrate phone
list.description: A short buzz you can feel, great with Shake camera. Works on Android phones; ignored on desktop and iPhone.

list.label: Place decal
list.hint: Stick a bullet hole, blood or scorch mark on a surface (from a collision it goes where it hit)

list.label: Set graphics quality
list.hint: One of the quality levels of the project (Low, Medium, High to start with): the project decides what each means

list.label: Set resolution scale
list.hint: Highest pixel ratio the screen is drawn at: lower is faster, blurrier

list.label: Set shadows
list.hint: Turn all shadows on or off

list.label: Set screen effects
list.hint: Glow, vignette, depth of field and the rest: switch them off to save speed

list.label: Set screen effect
list.hint: Change a setting of vignette, color, glow, depth of field or occlusion while playing (laid over the volumes), optionally gliding there

list.label: Switch screen effect on or off
list.hint: Edge smoothing, glow, depth of field or ambient occlusion

list.label: Set graphics option
list.hint: One setting of the quality level: switches take 1 (on) or 0 (off)

list.label: Set antialiasing (smooth edges)
list.hint: Smooth jagged edges. It can only change when the game starts, so a new value counts from the next start

list.label: Enter fullscreen
list.hint: Fill the screen (run it from a Button tap)

list.label: Exit fullscreen
list.hint: Go back to the normal window

list.label: Lock orientation
list.hint: Keep the screen landscape or portrait (run it from a Button tap)

list.label: Pause game
list.description: Freeze the game.

list.label: Resume game
list.description: Unfreeze the game.

list.label: Save value
list.hint: Keep a value on the device
list.description: Store a value on the device (kept after closing the game). Empty value = the variable with the same name as the key.

list.label: Load value
list.description: Read a saved value into a variable (nothing happens if it was never saved). Empty variable = same name as the key.

list.label: Set group active
list.description: Turn a group of events on or off.

list.label: Create object
list.description: Create a new object from a prefab (or copy of an object) at a position. It becomes picked for the next actions.

list.label: Start timer
list.description: Start a countdown. Use "On timer finished" to react when it ends.

list.label: Stop timer
list.description: Cancel a running timer.

list.label: Button is held
list.description: True while an on-screen button (or key) is held down.

list.label: On button pressed
list.description: True at the moment a button is pressed.

list.label: On button released
list.description: True at the moment a button is released.

list.label: On screen tapped
list.description: True when the player taps anywhere on the screen.

list.label: Screen is touched
list.description: True while a finger is on the screen.

list.label: On swipe
list.description: True when the player swipes in a direction.

list.label: Joystick is moving
list.description: True while the joystick (or WASD / arrows, or a gamepad stick) is pushed.

list.label: Joystick direction
list.description: True while the joystick is pushed in a direction.

list.label: Key is held
list.description: True while a keyboard key or gamepad button (PadA, PadB, PadX, PadY, PadLB, PadRB, PadLT, PadRT, PadStart…) is held.

list.label: On key pressed
list.description: True at the moment a keyboard key or gamepad button (PadA…) is pressed.

list.label: On collision with
list.description: Runs at the moment the object starts touching another object. In its actions, hitX, hitY, hitZ are where they touched, hitNormalX/Y/Z the surface direction (out of the other object toward this one), hitSpeed how fast they met and hitImpulse how hard they were pushed apart.

list.label: On collision ended
list.description: Runs at the moment two objects stop touching.

list.label: Is touching
list.description: True while the object touches (overlaps) another object. In its actions, hitX, hitY, hitZ, hitNormalX/Y/Z, hitSpeed and hitImpulse describe the current contact (for triggers hitX/Y/Z and the surface direction are estimated and hitImpulse is 0; all 0 when nothing touches).

list.label: Compare instance variable
list.description: Compare one of the object's own variables (e.g. hp).

list.label: Compare property
list.description: Compare position, angle, size or speed, e.g. Player y < -5.

list.label: Is on ground
list.description: True when a physics object is standing on something.

list.label: Is in a vehicle
list.description: True while the object rides a vehicle (after Enter vehicle).

list.label: Has a driver
list.description: True while someone is in this boat or car (after Enter vehicle).

list.label: Is in water
list.description: True while the object is inside a Water object — for a physics object, while any part of it is.

list.label: On enter water
list.description: Runs when a physics object enters a Water object, as soon as any part of it is under the surface.

list.label: On leave water
list.description: Runs when a physics object comes all the way out of a Water object.

list.label: Is emitting particles
list.description: True while its Particle System is making new particles.

list.label: Is playing particles
list.description: True while its Particle System plays: emitting, or particles still flying after a stop. False when paused or finished.

list.label: Is particles paused
list.description: True while its Particle System is paused ("Pause particles").

list.label: Compare particle count
list.description: How many of its particles are alive right now.

list.label: On particle collision
list.description: Runs when particles of the object hit another object. Needs its Collision module with "Send Collision Messages" on. In its actions, hitX, hitY, hitZ are where the first one hit, hitNormalX/Y/Z the surface direction and hitSpeed its speed after the hit.

list.label: On particles stopped
list.description: Runs when its Particle System has stopped and its last particle died. Needs "Stop Action" set to Callback in the Particle System.

list.label: Is playing animation
list.description: True while the given model animation is playing.

list.label: On hurt
list.description: Runs when the object (it needs the Health behavior) takes damage and survives or dies. Its health is in Self.health.

list.label: On death
list.description: Runs when the object’s health reaches 0 (it needs the Health behavior). It is still there during this event, then removed unless Destroy on death is off.

list.label: On arrived
list.description: Runs when the object reaches the point of its "Move to position" (or gets as close as it can when walls are in the way).

list.label: On reached end of curve
list.hint: Follow curve got to the end
list.display: On {object} reached the end of its curve

list.label: Is moving to a position
list.description: True while a "Move to position" is under way.

list.label: On animation finished
list.description: Runs when a play-once animation (loop off) reaches its end. Leave the name empty for any animation.

list.label: Has line of sight to
list.hint: Can see it, no wall between
list.description: True when nothing solid (walls, crates…) is between the object and the target, e.g. an enemy only chases the player it can see. Triggers (checkpoints, coins) never block the view.

list.label: Raycast from
list.hint: Shoot a ray out of it
list.description: Shoots a ray out of the object: forward, backward, left, right (the way it faces), or straight up or down. It never hits the object itself. Start height lifts the start above the object's center, e.g. to eye level. Uses the same rayHit…, rayNormal…, rayDistance and rayhitname() values and the same Must hit / Only tag / Ignore options as the Raycast condition. With several objects at once, the values come from the last one that hit.

list.label: Is moving
list.description: True when the object's physics speed is above zero.

list.label: Is tweening
list.description: True while a tween of that property is still running.

list.label: Is visible
list.description: True if the object is shown.

list.label: Has tag
list.description: True if the object has a tag.

list.label: On tapped
list.description: Runs when the player taps this object on screen (also works for UI buttons).

list.label: On created
list.description: Runs when a new instance of the object is created.

list.label: On destroyed
list.description: Runs when an instance of the object is destroyed.

list.label: Distance to
list.description: Compare the distance between the object and the nearest other object.

list.label: Compare count
list.description: Compare how many of this object exist (or are picked).

list.label: Exists
list.description: True if at least one of these objects exists. Invert it for "no more coins".

list.label: Pick nearest
list.description: Only use the instance closest to another object.

list.label: Pick farthest
list.description: Only use the instance farthest from another object.

list.label: Pick random
list.description: Only use one random instance.

list.label: For each
list.description: Run the actions and sub-events once for every instance, one at a time.

list.label: Destroy
list.description: Remove the object from the game.

list.label: Spawn object
list.description: Create an object (prefab) at this object's position (+ offset). The new object becomes picked for the next actions.

list.label: Set position
list.description: Teleport the object. Self.x means "keep the current x".

list.label: Move by
list.description: Move the object by an amount (world axes). Multiply by dt for smooth per-second movement.

list.label: Move forward
list.description: Move in the direction the object is facing.

list.label: Move toward object
list.description: Move toward another object (speed in meters per second).

list.label: Move toward position
list.description: Move toward a point (speed in meters per second).

list.label: Move to position
list.description: Walk to a point on the ground over the next frames (speed in meters per second), going around walls and rocks when "Go around walls" is on. A model plays its walk clip (sprint above "Sprint above speed") and idle when it stops, unless "Play walk / idle animations" is off. "On arrived" runs when it gets there. Tap to move: X = touchWorldX, Z = touchWorldZ.

list.label: Stop moving
list.description: Cancel a "Move to position" (it stays where it is, without "On arrived").

list.label: Set rotation
list.description: Set the rotation in degrees.

list.label: Set angle
list.description: Turn the object to face a direction (degrees around the vertical axis).

list.label: Rotate by
list.description: Turn the object by some degrees. Multiply by dt for smooth per-second rotation.

list.label: Look at
list.description: Turn the object to face another object.

list.label: Set size
list.description: Change the size (1 = normal).

list.label: Set visible
list.description: Show or hide the object.

list.label: Set enabled
list.description: A disabled object is hidden and stops moving/colliding.

list.label: Set color
list.hint: Tint it, e.g. red when hit
list.description: Change the object's color.

list.label: Set opacity
list.description: 1 = solid, 0 = invisible.

list.label: Set shader uniform
list.hint: A setting of the custom shader: a number, or a colour like "#ff0000"

list.label: Focus depth of field on object
list.hint: Keep this object sharp: the depth-of-field focus follows how far it is from the camera

list.label: Set volume profile
list.hint: Put another post-processing profile on a Post-processing Volume (empty = none)
list.description: Put another post-processing profile on a Post-processing Volume (empty = none).

list.label: Set volume weight
list.hint: How much of a Post-processing Volume counts: 0 = none, 1 = all
list.display: Set {object} volume weight to {weight} over {seconds} s
list.description: How much of a Post-processing Volume counts: 0 = none, 1 = all.

list.label: Tween
list.description: Smoothly animate position, angle, size or opacity to a value, e.g. size 1.5 with Back for a pop, or Self.y + 2 to rise. Starting another tween of the same property replaces it. On a UI element, x and y are its position on the screen (in canvas pixels, from its anchor), angle its rotation, size its scale and opacity its fade (children follow); z does nothing.

list.label: Set morph target
list.hint: Bend a model: a smile, open mouth, a door bending open
list.display: Set {object} morph target {name} to {value} in {seconds} s

list.label: Video
list.hint: Play, pause or restart the video on its surface

list.label: Stop tweens
list.description: Stop every running tween of the object where it is now.

list.label: Attach to
list.description: The object becomes a child of the target and moves with it, e.g. a key the player picked up. It stays where it is; use Set position afterwards to place it relative to the target (0, 0, 0 = the center of the target).

list.label: Enter vehicle
list.hint: Pick the player, then the boat or car
list.description: The object (usually the player) gets into a vehicle — an object with the Boat or Car behavior: it sits in the vehicle’s Seat and rides along, its own movement stops and cameras following it follow the vehicle (the vehicle’s Auto seat and Auto camera settings switch these off if you do them yourself). It does not steer the vehicle: pass the input in with Drive car / Move with input. Undo it all with Exit vehicle.

list.label: Exit vehicle
list.description: Gets out of the vehicle it is in: it is put down beside it (on land if one side has some) and moves on its own again; the vehicle stops being driven.

list.label: Drive car
list.description: Drives a Car (Driver "manual"): steer −1 (left) … 1 (right), gas 0 … 1, brake 0 … 1. Use it every tick the controls are held (e.g. under "On button Gas held"); when the event stops running the car coasts. Works with your own buttons, a touch wheel or anything else in events.

list.label: Move with input
list.description: Moves the object like the joystick does, from events: x −1 (left) … 1 (right), y −1 (back) … 1 (forward). Works for a Platformer, Top-down movement or a Boat. They never read the joystick themselves, so pass it in: x = joystickX, y = joystickY. Use it every tick the input is held (e.g. under "On button Left held"); when it stops, the object stops.

list.label: Simulate control
list.description: Presses one of the movement controls for this tick, like the joystick or a key would: Left / Right steer and strafe, Up is gas / forward, Down is brake / reverse, Jump jumps, Handbrake locks the wheels. Use it every tick the control is held (e.g. under "On button Left held"). Several at once in the same tick stack up, so Left + Up steers and accelerates together. Works on Platformer, Top-down, Car and Boat. They never read the joystick themselves: this and Move with input / Drive car are the only things that move them.

list.label: Detach
list.description: Let go of an attached object: it stays where it is and moves on its own again.

list.label: Call script function
list.hint: Run an exported function of a code script
list.description: Run a function from one of the object's code scripts. In the script, write "export function name(a, b) {…}". Fill only the arguments the function takes. To use its result in a condition or value, write Object.script("Script", "name", a, b) in an expression.

list.label: Set instance variable
list.description: Change one of the object's own variables.

list.label: Add to instance variable
list.description: Increase one of the object's own variables.

list.label: Subtract from instance variable
list.description: Decrease one of the object's own variables.

list.label: Set spin
list.hint: Degrees per second around the world X, Y and Z axes; the body must be allowed to tip over

list.label: Set velocity
list.description: Set the physics speed on each axis (needs a Rigid body).

list.label: Push (impulse)
list.description: Give the object a sudden push (needs a Rigid body).

list.label: Break joint
list.hint: Cut its Joint (rope snaps, door torn off)

list.label: Apply force
list.description: Push continuously (use every tick; needs a Rigid body).

list.label: Jump
list.description: Jump up, only when standing on the ground (needs a Rigid body).

list.label: Set curve progress
list.hint: Jump to a place on the curve

list.label: Damage
list.description: Take health from the object (it needs the Health behavior). "From" is what hit it, e.g. Bullet: with Knockback on, it is pushed away from that.

list.label: Heal
list.description: Give the object health back, up to its Max health (it needs the Health behavior).

list.label: Set text
list.description: Change the text shown by a text object.

list.label: Set text
list.description: Change the text of an object with a Text component, e.g. "Score: " + Score.

list.label: Append text
list.description: Add text at the end of the current text.

list.label: Play animation
list.hint: Play a model or sprite animation
list.description: Play a clip of its 3D model, e.g. "walk", "jump" or "die". Loop off = play once and hold the last frame.

list.label: Ragdoll
list.hint: Make a rigged character limp: it falls and tumbles with physics (use it for a death)

list.label: Set ragdoll power
list.hint: How hard a ragdoll follows its animation: 0 = limp, 1 = holds the animation (a hit still moves it)

list.label: Push ragdoll part
list.hint: Push the limp character's bones whose name contains the text (head, arm, leg)

list.label: Stop animation
list.description: Stop the playing model animation.

list.label: Set animation speed
list.description: 1 = normal, 0.5 = half speed, 2 = double.

list.label: Set sprite frame
list.hint: Show one frame of a sprite

list.label: Set tile
list.hint: Paint one cell of a tilemap

list.label: Erase tile
list.hint: Empty one cell of a tilemap
list.display: Erase the tile at cell ({x}, {y}) of {object}

list.label: Burst particles
list.description: Shoot some particles at once, e.g. sparks on a hit or a puff on landing. Needs a Particles component.

list.label: Emit particles with values
list.description: Shoot particles at once with values of your own instead of those of the Particle System: a velocity (x, y, z in its simulation space: own space for Local, world space for World), size, lifetime or color. Leave a field empty to use that setting of the Particle System; an empty velocity axis counts as 0 once any axis is filled. A position (same space as the velocity) starts them there instead of at the emitter, e.g. at hitX, hitY, hitZ; an empty position axis counts as 0 once any axis is filled.

list.label: Spawn particles here
list.description: Play a ready-made effect once where the object is, e.g. Sparkles when a coin is collected (works even if you destroy it right after). No Particles component needed.

list.label: Start particles
list.description: Start its Particles component. Running it while the emitter is already going has no effect, so it can sit under a condition that holds for many ticks; a one-shot effect such as Explosion plays again once the previous one has finished.

list.label: Restart particles
list.description: Play its Particles component from the beginning, even if it is already going (bursts again).

list.label: Stop particles
list.description: Stop making new particles. The ones already flying finish their life, or go at once.

list.label: Pause particles
list.description: Freeze its particles where they are. "Start particles" carries on from there.

list.label: Clear particles
list.description: Remove every particle it has out right now (it keeps emitting if it was).

list.label: Set particle start color
list.description: The color new particles start with (Color over Lifetime still multiplies it).

list.label: Set particle start value
list.description: A start value of new particles: speed (m/s), size (m), lifetime (s), rotation (degrees), gravity modifier, or how fast the whole system runs.

list.label: Turn particle module on/off
list.description: Switch one module of its Particle System on or off while the game runs.

list.label: Set particle rate
list.description: How many particles it makes per second, e.g. a bigger fire or a stronger engine trail.

list.label: Play its sound
list.description: Play the sound of the object's Audio component.

list.label: Stop its sound
list.description: Stop the sound of the object's Audio component.

list.label: Enable/disable behavior
list.description: Turn one of the object's behaviors on or off.

list.label: Set behavior setting
list.description: Change a behavior setting, e.g. platformer speed.

list.label: Keep across scenes
list.hint: Make it come along to the next scene instead of being made again (with its children, position and variables)

list.label: Set layer
list.hint: Move it to a layer (Project settings → Layers): cameras can leave layers out, raycasts can look at only some

list.label: Add tag
list.description: Give the object a tag.

list.label: Remove tag
list.description: Remove a tag from the object.

list.label: On state entered
list.description: Runs when the object's Animator starts a state: as the cross-fade into it begins. Leave the name empty for any state.

list.label: On state exited
list.description: Runs when the object's Animator has left a state: as the cross-fade out of it ends. Leave the name empty for any state.

list.label: Is in state
list.description: True while the object's Animator is in that state of its Base Layer (during a cross-fade, the state it is going to).

list.label: Compare parameter
list.description: Compares one of the Animator's parameters with a value. A bool reads as 1 or 0.

list.label: Set parameter
list.description: Sets a float, int or bool parameter of the object's Animator. Its transitions check it in the same frame.

list.label: Set trigger
list.description: Sets a trigger parameter. The next transition that tests it is taken and uses it up.

list.label: Reset trigger
list.description: Unsets a trigger that no transition has used yet.

list.label: Play state
list.description: Goes to a state straight away, or cross-fades into it over the time given. Layer 0 is the Base Layer; a layer name works too.

list.label: Set layer weight
list.description: How much a layer of the Animator counts: 0 = not at all, 1 = fully. The Base Layer always counts fully.

list.label: On timeline signal
list.hint: A marker on a timeline's Signals track was reached

list.label: On timeline finished
list.hint: A timeline played to its end

list.label: Timeline is playing
list.hint: e.g. to block input during a cutscene

list.label: Play timeline
list.hint: Start a cutscene (resumes a paused one)

list.label: Stop timeline
list.hint: Back to the start; the camera is given back

list.label: Skip timeline
list.hint: A Skip button: jump to the end, the signals still to come fire

list.label: Jump to time
list.hint: Go to a second without firing what lies between

list.label: Render texture
list.hint: Freeze or restart the picture a camera draws into a render texture, or draw it once

list.label: Set language
list.hint: Every text with a key changes; remembered for next time

list.label: Set text from key
list.hint: Its text in the current language, from Files → Localization
list.display: Set {object} text to the text of key {key}

list.label: Add achievement steps
list.hint: Unlocks when all steps are done

list.label: Show rewarded ad
list.hint: Then use On rewarded ad earned

list.label: On rewarded ad earned
list.hint: The player watched it to the end

list.label: Send web request
list.hint: Then use On web response (reply: webjson("score"), webtext(), webstatus())

list.label: On web error
list.hint: A request failed: blocked, no network, too slow, or not a 2xx reply (weberror() says why)

list.label: Create room
list.hint: Then use On room joined, and give netcode() to your friends
list.display: Create room as {name}, up to {max} players

list.label: Join room
list.hint: With the code a friend got from netcode()

list.label: Send message
list.hint: To every other player; read it with netdata() in On message (netdata("0"), netdata("1") when it carries several values)

list.label: Spawn for everyone
list.hint: Every player in the room sees it; you drive it, the others see a copy that follows. Outside a room it just spawns

list.label: Is mine
list.hint: You drive this object: a placed object belongs to the host, a spawned one belongs to whoever spawned it. Always true outside a room

list.label: I am the host
list.hint: The player who has been in the room the longest

list.label: On room joined
list.hint: You made or joined a room

list.label: On room failed
list.hint: Could not join: neterror() says why (notfound, full, busy, offline)

list.label: On player joined
list.hint: Another player came in: netwho() is their name

list.label: On player left
list.hint: A player left: netwho() is their name

list.label: On message
list.hint: Another player sent one: netdata() is what it carries, netwho() who sent it

list.label: On disconnected
list.hint: The connection to the room was lost

list.label: On clicked
list.description: Runs when the player taps a UI button (e.g. Start, Pause, Retry).

list.label: Is held down
list.description: True while the player holds a UI button (e.g. a custom fire button).

list.label: Compare slider value
list.hint: Check a slider or bar value
list.description: Compare the value of a slider or bar, e.g. Health value ≤ 0.

list.label: On value changed
list.description: Runs when the player drags a slider to a new value (e.g. a volume setting).

list.label: Show
list.description: Show a UI element or a whole screen (and everything inside it).

list.label: Hide
list.description: Hide a UI element or a whole screen.

list.label: Show / hide
list.description: Show it if hidden, hide it if shown.

list.label: Set label
list.description: Change the text of a label or button, e.g. "Lives: " + Lives.

list.label: Set position
list.hint: Offset from its anchors. To land on another element, use Move to element
list.description: Move a UI element on the screen: x (right) and y (up) are its Rect Transform’s anchored position, in canvas pixels from its anchor, the same numbers as in the inspector. Leave a field empty to keep that axis. For a smooth slide use Tween (x / y) instead.

list.label: Set screen position
list.hint: Puts its pivot there. To land on another element use its centerX, centerY

list.label: Set anchors
list.hint: Where it hangs in its parent (0 to 1)

list.label: Set pivot
list.hint: The point it turns and sits around (0 to 1)

list.label: Put inside
list.hint: Move into another element, e.g. a slot or list

list.label: Set slider value
list.description: Set a slider or bar value, e.g. health or time left.

list.label: Add to slider value
list.description: Add (or subtract with a negative number) to a slider. Stays between its min and max.

list.label: Set slider maximum
list.description: Set the maximum of a slider.

list.label: Set slider minimum
list.description: Set the minimum of a slider (0 by default).

list.label: Enable / disable
list.description: Grey out a button or slider so it takes no input, or turn it back on (Interactable).

list.label: Set image
list.description: Change the picture of an image, button or panel.

list.label: Set font
list.hint: Change the font of its text
list.description: Change the font of a label or a button's text to a font in Files. Leave it empty for the default font.

list.label: Set background color
list.description: Change the background color of a button, panel or bar.

list.label: Set text color
list.description: Change the text color of a label or button.

list.label: Set bar color
list.description: Change the fill color of a slider or bar.

list.label: Show
list.description: Show an on-screen control button (Scene → Controls) hidden with Hide.

list.label: Hide
list.description: Hide an on-screen control button (Scene → Controls). A hidden button can’t be pressed — not with a finger, keys or a gamepad — so it only works where it makes sense, e.g. only while the player touches the boat.

list.label: Set label
list.description: Change the text on an on-screen control button, e.g. “Board” next to the boat and “Leave” while sailing.

list.label: Play sound
list.description: Play a sound from your assets.

list.label: Stop sound
list.description: Stop a sound (leave empty to stop all sounds).

list.label: Is sound playing
list.description: True while a sound you played (or any, when empty) is still playing. A sound that is fading out no longer counts.

list.label: Play music
list.description: Plays music, one track at a time: another track cross-fades from the one playing; the same track only changes its volume. Loops unless you turn Loop off.

list.label: Stop music
list.description: Fades the music out over the time given.

list.label: Is music playing
list.description: True while music (or that music) is playing.

list.label: Set master volume
list.description: 0 = silent, 1 = full volume.

list.label: Set group volume
list.description: Sets the volume of a group of the audio mixer (Project settings → Audio mixer), faded over the time given. Master is the master volume.

list.label: Mute group
list.description: Silences a mixer group, or brings it back at its volume.

list.label: Set group low-pass
list.description: Muffles a mixer group with a low-pass filter (Hz; 0 = off), e.g. 600 under water.

list.label: Pause all sounds
list.description: Pauses every sound where it is, for a pause menu. Resume all sounds carries on.

list.label: Resume all sounds
list.description: Carries on the sounds paused by Pause all sounds.

list.label: Shake camera
list.description: Shake the screen, great for hits and explosions.

list.label: Camera look at
list.description: Turn the main camera toward an object.

list.label: Set camera position
list.description: Move the main camera.

list.label: Draw point
list.description: Debug: draw a small cross at a position to see where it is, e.g. at Enemy.x, Enemy.y, Enemy.z. Shapes are drawn over the game and are for testing.

list.label: Draw line
list.hint: Debug: a line between two points
list.description: Debug: draw a line between two positions, e.g. from the Player to the Target, to check distances and directions.

list.label: Draw sphere
list.description: Debug: draw a wire sphere to see a range or radius, e.g. how far an enemy notices you.

list.label: Draw circle
list.hint: Debug: a ring on the ground
list.description: Debug: draw a ring lying flat on the ground at a position, e.g. an area or a spawn radius.

list.label: Draw box
list.description: Debug: draw a wire box around a position to check a size or an area, e.g. a trigger zone.

list.label: Spawn particles
list.description: Play a ready-made effect once at a position, e.g. an Explosion at Enemy.x, Enemy.y, Enemy.z. No object needed.
